_README: Destinations content. Place names & facts are real; descriptions are editorial. Any hard number (visitor stats) comes from data/facts.json via factId. No invented hours/prices/distances.

myeongdong.name: Myeongdong
myeongdong.blurb: Shopping, street food and beauty — the classic first stop.
intro: Myeongdong is Seoul's busiest shopping street and the most-visited area for foreign travelers. It's packed with cosmetics shops, fashion, and a lively evening street-food scene.
It's central and easy to reach, which makes it a natural base or first stop on day one.
tips: Come hungry in the evening — the street-food carts are the highlight.
Beauty shops often give free samples; compare a few before buying.
Line 4 Myeongdong Station, exits 5–8, drop you in the middle of it.

gyeongbokgung.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace
gyeongbokgung.blurb: Grand royal palace — wear a hanbok for free entry.
intro: Gyeongbokgung is the largest of Seoul's Joseon-era royal palaces, with grand gates, courtyards and a scenic pavilion over a pond.
Renting a hanbok (traditional dress) nearby lets you enter free and makes for memorable photos.
tips: Wear a hanbok for free palace entry.
Try to catch the changing-of-the-guard ceremony at the main gate.
Bukchon Hanok Village is a short walk away — pair them in one morning.

n-seoul-tower.name: N Seoul Tower
n-seoul-tower.blurb: Namsan cable car and the city's best skyline.
intro: Perched atop Namsan mountain, N Seoul Tower gives the best panoramic view over the city, especially at sunset and after dark.
The Namsan cable car up the hill is part of the fun.
tips: Go near sunset to catch both day and night views.
Take the cable car up; you can walk down through Namsan Park.
Weekends and holidays get busy — arrive early or late.

bukchon.name: Bukchon Hanok Village
bukchon.blurb: Traditional hanok lanes and photogenic viewpoints.
intro: Bukchon is a hillside neighborhood of preserved hanok (traditional houses) between two palaces, with quiet lanes and rooftop views.
It's a living residential area, so it rewards a calm, respectful stroll.
tips: Keep your voice down — people live here.
Mornings are quietest for photos.
Combine with Gyeongbokgung and Insadong nearby.

hongdae.name: Hongdae
hongdae.blurb: Street performances, indie shops and nightlife.
intro: Hongdae, around Hongik University, is Seoul's youthful arts-and-music district — buskers, indie boutiques, clubs and late-night eats.
It's the place to feel the city's energy after dark.
tips: Evenings bring out the street performers.
Explore the side streets for cafes and vintage shops.
Well connected by Line 2 and the AREX airport line.

seongsu.name: Seongsu
seongsu.blurb: Seoul's trendiest coffee and dessert street.
intro: Once an industrial area, Seongsu is now Seoul's coolest café and design district — converted warehouses, roasteries and pop-up stores.
Travelers from the Americas especially gravitate here.
tips: Cafe-hop; many roasters are within a few blocks.
Weekdays are calmer than weekends.
Pair with Seoul Forest park next door.

bukhansan.name: Bukhansan (K-Hiking)
bukhansan.blurb: Granite peaks on the city's edge — Korea's fastest-growing trend.
intro: Bukhansan National Park rises right at Seoul's edge, with granite peaks and temple trails — and it leads the surging 'K-hiking' trend among foreign visitors.
Trails range from easy walks to steep scrambles, so pick one to match your fitness.
tips: Start early in the morning, especially in summer.
Wear proper shoes; upper sections are rocky.
Check the weather and carry water.

dmz.name: DMZ Tour
dmz.blurb: The border zone — visited on an organized tour.
intro: The Demilitarized Zone between South and North Korea is a striking day trip from Seoul, usually done via an organized tour that handles access and rules.
Stops can include observatories and infiltration tunnels.
tips: You must join an authorized tour — you can't go independently.
Bring your passport; there are ID checks.
Book ahead, especially in peak season.

haeundae.name: Haeundae Beach
haeundae.blurb: Busan's most famous beach and seaside district.
intro: Haeundae is Busan's signature beach — a long sandy stretch backed by hotels, cafés and the Blueline Park coastal rail with its colorful sky capsules.
It's the easiest base for a first Busan trip.
tips: The Blueline Park sky capsule is popular — book ahead in season.
Nearby Gwangalli Beach is best at night for the Diamond Bridge lights.
Seafood restaurants line the back streets.

gamcheon.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
gamcheon.blurb: Hillside village of brightly painted houses.
intro: Gamcheon is a photogenic hillside neighborhood of pastel houses, murals and art installations, often called Busan's 'Santorini'.
Narrow stepped lanes reward slow wandering.
tips: Wear comfortable shoes — it's hilly with lots of steps.
Follow the art-map stamp trail for the best routes.
It's a residential area, so keep noise down.

jagalchi.name: Jagalchi Fish Market
intro: Jagalchi is Korea's largest seafood market — pick your catch downstairs and have it prepared upstairs.
It's a lively, authentic slice of Busan's port life.
tips: Go for lunch when it's freshest and busiest.
Prices are often negotiable — agree before you order.
Combine with Gukje Market and BIFF Square next door.

seongsan.name: Seongsan Ilchulbong
seongsan.blurb: UNESCO sunrise peak on Jeju's east coast.
intro: Seongsan Ilchulbong ('Sunrise Peak') is a dramatic volcanic tuff cone rising from the sea, a UNESCO World Heritage site and Jeju's signature sunrise spot.
The climb to the crater rim is short but steep.
tips: Sunrise is the classic time, but any clear day is stunning.
It's a real climb — wear good shoes.
Pair with Seopjikoji and Manjanggul on an east-Jeju day.

hallasan.name: Hallasan
hallasan.blurb: Jeju's volcano — trails for every level.
intro: Hallasan is a shield volcano at the center of Jeju and the highest mountain in South Korea, ringed by trails through changing forest and alpine scenery.
Some summit trails require an early start and reservations.
tips: Check which trails reach the summit and whether reservations are needed.
Weather changes fast — bring layers.
Start early to finish within park hours.

changdeokgung.name: Changdeokgung Palace
changdeokgung.blurb: UNESCO palace with the famous Secret Garden.
intro: Changdeokgung is the best-preserved of Seoul’s Joseon-era royal palaces and a UNESCO World Heritage site, laid out to follow the natural hillside rather than impose on it.
Its Huwon ‘Secret Garden’, seen on a timed guided walk, is the highlight — especially in autumn.
tips: The Secret Garden (Huwon) uses a separate timed ticket — book or arrive early.
Like other palaces it closes one day a week; check hours on the official site.
It pairs naturally with Bukchon and Gyeongbokgung in one morning.

ddp.name: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP)
ddp.blurb: Zaha Hadid’s flowing landmark and night market.
intro: The Dongdaemun Design Plaza, designed by Zaha Hadid, is a sweeping silver landmark of curves with barely a straight line — Seoul’s hub for design, exhibitions and fashion.
The surrounding Dongdaemun district is a round-the-clock shopping area, liveliest late at night.
tips: It is most photogenic after dark, when the building and LED rose garden light up.
Exhibitions rotate — check what is on before you go.
The night-market fashion malls nearby run into the early hours.

lotte-world-tower.name: Lotte World Tower
lotte-world-tower.blurb: Korea’s tallest tower — the Seoul Sky observation deck.
intro: Lotte World Tower in Jamsil is the tallest building in South Korea, with the Seoul Sky observation decks near the top for sweeping views over the city and the Han River.
At its base are a huge mall, an aquarium and a concert hall, with the Lotte World theme park next door.
tips: Go on a clear day for the Seoul Sky view; sunset is popular.
Book Seoul Sky tickets ahead to skip the queue.
Seokchon Lake beside it is lovely in cherry-blossom season.

ikseondong.name: Ikseon-dong
ikseondong.blurb: Restored hanok alleys of cafes and boutiques.
intro: Ikseon-dong is a maze of narrow lanes where century-old hanok houses have been restored into cafes, dessert shops, boutiques and small restaurants.
It is a compact, atmospheric pocket that blends old architecture with a young, design-led scene.
tips: Come to wander slowly and cafe-hop — it is small but dense.
Weekday afternoons are calmer than weekends.
It is a short walk from Jongno-3-ga station and Insadong.

yonggungsa.name: Haedong Yonggungsa
yonggungsa.blurb: A rare Buddhist temple right on the sea.
intro: Haedong Yonggungsa is one of Korea’s few seaside temples, its shrines and pagodas built onto the rocks just above the waves on Busan’s northeast coast.
The mix of sea, cliffs and temple makes it especially striking at sunrise.
tips: Sunrise and early morning are the most peaceful times.
There are many steps down to the temple and back up.
Combine it with the coastal spots on an east-Busan day.

taejongdae.name: Taejongdae
taejongdae.blurb: Cliff-top park with sea views and a lighthouse.
intro: Taejongdae is a forested coastal park on the southern tip of Busan’s Yeongdo island, ringed by dramatic sea cliffs, a lighthouse and viewpoints over open water.
A road train loops the park for those who would rather not walk the whole hilly circuit.
tips: Take the Danubi road train if you would rather not walk the hilly loop.
The observatory and lighthouse have the best views.
On clear days you can sometimes see distant islands.

songdo.name: Songdo Beach
songdo.blurb: Historic beach with an air-cruise cable car.
intro: Songdo is one of Korea’s oldest public beaches, now best known for the Songdo Air Cruise cable car gliding out over the bay and a curving cloud-trail skywalk along the shore.
It is a relaxed, family-friendly alternative to busier Haeundae.
tips: The cable car has standard and glass-floor ‘crystal’ cabins.
Walk the seaside skywalk for photos out over the water.
It is a short hop from Nampo-dong and Jagalchi.

jusangjeolli.name: Jusangjeolli Cliffs
jusangjeolli.blurb: Hexagonal basalt columns above the sea.
intro: The Jusangjeolli Cliffs on Jeju’s south coast are a wall of dark, hexagonal basalt columns formed as lava met the sea, with waves crashing against the stacked stone.
A short boardwalk leads to viewpoints over the formation.
tips: Rougher-sea days make the waves against the columns more dramatic.
It is an easy, flat walk from the parking area.
Pair it with the Jungmun resort area and Cheonjiyeon Waterfall nearby.

insadong.name: Insadong
insadong.blurb: Antiques, tea houses and traditional crafts.
intro: Insadong is Seoul’s traditional-culture street, lined with antique shops, art galleries, craft stores, tea houses and calligraphy studios.
Its main lane and side alleys are pedestrian-friendly and easy to browse on foot.
tips: Duck into the side alleys for tea houses and hidden courtyards.
The Ssamziegil complex spirals upward with small craft shops.
It is an easy walk from Gyeongbokgung and Bukchon.

gwangjang-market.name: Gwangjang Market
gwangjang-market.blurb: One of Seoul’s oldest street-food markets.
intro: Gwangjang Market is one of Seoul’s oldest traditional markets, famous for its buzzing street-food alley.
Grab a stool for bindaetteok (mung-bean pancakes), mayak gimbap and other classics.
tips: Come hungry and share several dishes across stalls.
Lunchtime and early evening are liveliest.
Many food stalls prefer cash.

gwangalli.name: Gwangalli Beach
gwangalli.blurb: Beach with the Gwangan Bridge light show.
intro: Gwangalli is a relaxed city beach framed by the Gwangan ‘Diamond’ Bridge, whose nightly light show makes it Busan’s favourite after-dark spot.
A young strip of cafes, bars and seafood restaurants lines the sand.
tips: Come at night for the bridge light show, and drone shows on some weekends.
The cafe-and-bar strip is livelier than Haeundae’s.
It is a short subway hop from Haeundae.

cheonjiyeon.name: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall
cheonjiyeon.blurb: Lush waterfall in the heart of Seogwipo.
intro: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall tumbles into a wide pool at the end of a short, lush trail in Seogwipo on Jeju’s south coast.
The subtropical gorge around it stays green year-round and is lit at night.
tips: The walk in is short, flat and stroller-friendly.
Evenings bring illuminations along the path.
Pair it with Jusangjeolli and the Jungmun area nearby.

manjanggul.name: Manjanggul Cave
manjanggul.blurb: A vast UNESCO lava tube you can walk through.
intro: Manjanggul is one of the world’s finest lava tubes and part of Jeju’s UNESCO World Heritage listing, formed by flowing volcanic lava.
An open section leads through the tunnel to a towering lava column.
tips: It stays cool inside year-round — bring a light layer.
The floor is uneven and damp; wear grippy shoes.
It is on the east side, near Seongsan.

bulguksa.name: Bulguksa Temple
intro: Bulguksa is a masterpiece of Silla-era Buddhist art and a UNESCO World Heritage site, with stone terraces, bridges and two celebrated pagodas.
It is the centrepiece of a visit to Gyeongju, Korea’s ancient capital.
tips: Pair it with the Seokguram Grotto up the same mountain.
Mornings are quietest and best for photos.
Autumn colour around the temple is spectacular.

cheomseongdae.name: Cheomseongdae Observatory
cheomseongdae.blurb: One of Asia’s oldest surviving observatories.
intro: Cheomseongdae is a bottle-shaped stone tower from the Silla kingdom, regarded as one of the oldest surviving astronomical observatories in Asia.
It stands among royal tombs and seasonal flower fields in central Gyeongju.
tips: The surrounding Wolseong parkland is lovely at dusk.
It is floodlit and photogenic after dark.
Combine it with Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond next door.

wolji.name: Donggung Palace & Wolji Pond
wolji.blurb: Silla palace ruins mirrored in a night-lit pond.
intro: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond (formerly Anapji) are the restored grounds of a Silla royal pleasure garden, most magical after dark.
Illuminated pavilions reflect in the still water — Gyeongju’s signature night view.
tips: Come after sunset for the famous reflections.
It is a short walk from Cheomseongdae.
Check the closing time so you do not miss the evening view.

cheonggyecheon.name: Cheonggyecheon Stream
cheonggyecheon.blurb: A restored stream cutting through downtown Seoul.
intro: Cheonggyecheon is a restored stream that runs through the heart of Seoul, sunk below street level as a long walking park.
Once buried under a highway, it is now a cool, green escape with stepping stones, fountains and seasonal light displays.
tips: It is a refreshing walk on a hot day — the water keeps it cooler.
Evenings bring lantern and light installations, especially in winter.
Start near Gwanghwamun / Cheonggye Plaza and follow it east.

huinnyeoul.name: Huinnyeoul Culture Village
huinnyeoul.blurb: Whitewashed lanes on a seaside cliff.
intro: Huinnyeoul Culture Village clings to a cliff on Busan’s Yeongdo island, its white houses and narrow lanes looking straight out over the sea.
A coastal path runs below the village along the water’s edge.
tips: Walk both the upper lanes and the lower seaside path.
It is a residential area — keep noise down.
Combine it with Taejongdae on Yeongdo.

udo.name: Udo Island
udo.blurb: A tiny island of beaches and coastal cycling.
intro: Udo (‘Cow Island’) is a small islet off Jeju’s east coast, reached by a short ferry and best explored by bike, scooter or the island bus.
White-and-turquoise beaches, low stone walls and sea views make it a relaxed half-day trip.
tips: Take the ferry from near Seongsan; it is a short crossing.
Rent a bike or electric scooter to loop the island.
Go early to beat day-trip crowds in peak season.

jeonju-hanok.name: Jeonju Hanok Village
jeonju-hanok.blurb: Korea’s best-known hanok village and food capital.
intro: Jeonju Hanok Village is a large, well-preserved neighbourhood of traditional hanok houses in the city that gave the world bibimbap.
Its lanes are packed with tea houses, craft workshops, hanbok rentals and street food.
tips: Try Jeonju-style bibimbap and the local street food.
Rent a hanbok to wander the lanes.
It is an easy trip from Seoul by fast train and bus.

gyeonggijeon.name: Gyeonggijeon Shrine
gyeonggijeon.blurb: Serene shrine beside the hanok village.
intro: Gyeonggijeon is a tranquil walled shrine holding a portrait of King Taejo, founder of the Joseon dynasty, right beside Jeonju Hanok Village.
Its bamboo groves and old halls are a calm counterpoint to the busy lanes outside.
tips: It pairs naturally with a Jeonju Hanok Village visit.
The bamboo grove and rear gardens are the highlight.
The nearby Jeondong Catholic Cathedral is worth a look.

gyeongpo.name: Gyeongpo Beach
gyeongpo.blurb: Gangneung’s wide beach and coffee scene.
intro: Gyeongpo is Gangneung’s long, wide East Sea beach, backed by pine groves, a scenic lake and one of Korea’s best-known coffee cultures.
It is the summer favourite of the east coast, an easy fast-train ride from Seoul.
tips: The cafe strip along Anmok beach is famous for coffee.
Gyeongpo Lake beside the beach is lovely for a cherry-blossom walk.
Summer weekends are busy — arrive early.

jeongdongjin.name: Jeongdongjin
jeongdongjin.blurb: Famous sunrise beach with a seaside railway.
intro: Jeongdongjin is a small east-coast town known for sunrises over the sea and a railway station that sits right on the beach.
A hilltop sail-shaped hotel and an hourglass park add to its quirky charm.
tips: It is a classic spot to watch the New Year sunrise.
The station is one of the closest to the sea anywhere.
Reachable by train down the east coast from Gangneung.

hwaseong.name: Hwaseong Fortress
hwaseong.blurb: UNESCO fortress walls circling old Suwon.
intro: Hwaseong is a grand Joseon-era fortress wall that rings the old centre of Suwon, a UNESCO World Heritage site of gates, watchtowers and floodgates.
You can walk the full circuit of the walls for ever-changing views over the city.
tips: Walk a section of the wall between the grand gates.
A trolley and archery experiences run inside the fortress.
It is a short train ride south of Seoul.

daereungwon.name: Daereungwon Tomb Complex
daereungwon.blurb: Grassy royal burial mounds of ancient Silla.
intro: Daereungwon is a park of large grassy burial mounds holding the tombs of Silla kings and nobles in the heart of Gyeongju.
One mound, Cheonmachong, is open inside to show excavated treasures and a famous painted saddle flap.
tips: Cheonmachong is the one tomb you can step inside.
The mounds are lovely at dusk and in cherry-blossom season.
It is walking distance from Cheomseongdae and the Hwangnidan-gil street.

jaman.name: Jaman Mural Village
jaman.blurb: A hillside of alleys covered in murals.
intro: Jaman Mural Village climbs a hill on the edge of Jeonju Hanok Village, its narrow lanes and old walls painted with colourful murals.
Small cafes and craft shops tuck in between the artworks.
tips: It is a short but steep walk up from the hanok village.
Great for photos and a quiet coffee away from the crowds.
Wear comfortable shoes for the slopes.

ojukheon.name: Ojukheon
ojukheon.blurb: One of Korea’s oldest surviving wooden houses.
intro: Ojukheon in Gangneung is the birthplace of the Joseon scholar Yi I and his mother, the artist Shin Saimdang — both featured on Korean banknotes.
It is one of the oldest surviving wooden homes in the country, set in a quiet garden of black bamboo.
tips: Look for the black-bamboo grove that gives the house its name.
There is a small museum on the grounds.
Pair it with Gyeongpo Beach and lake nearby.

haenggung.name: Hwaseong Haenggung Palace
haenggung.blurb: The detached palace inside Hwaseong Fortress.
intro: Hwaseong Haenggung was a temporary palace where the king stayed when visiting Suwon — the largest of Joseon’s detached palaces, set within Hwaseong Fortress.
Restored courtyards and halls host changing-of-the-guard and martial-arts performances.
tips: Check the schedule for guard-ceremony and martial-arts shows.
Combine it with a walk on the Hwaseong walls.
It is a short train ride south of Seoul.

starfield-coex.name: Starfield Library (COEX)
starfield-coex.blurb: A soaring open library inside COEX Mall.
intro: The Starfield Library is a vast, open two-storey library at the heart of the COEX Mall in Gangnam, with towering shelves that have made it one of Seoul’s most photographed spots.
The mall around it holds shops, an aquarium and the SMTOWN K-pop complex.
tips: It is free to enter and browse.
Weekday mornings are quietest for photos.
K-pop fans can visit SMTOWN in the same complex.

oryukdo.name: Oryukdo Skywalk
oryukdo.blurb: Glass-floor walkway over the sea cliffs.
intro: The Oryukdo Skywalk is a horseshoe-shaped glass walkway jutting out from the cliffs at the southern tip of Busan, above the rocky Oryukdo islets.
It marks the point where Korea’s South Sea meets the East Sea.
tips: You put on slippers over your shoes to protect the glass.
Clear days give the best views of the islets.
The nearby Igidae coastal trail is worth the extra time.

seoraksan.name: Seoraksan National Park
seoraksan.blurb: Granite peaks, temples and autumn colour.
intro: Seoraksan is Korea’s most famous national park — dramatic granite peaks, valleys and temples near the east-coast city of Sokcho.
A cable car climbs toward Gwongeumseong fortress, and trails of every level fan out from Sinheungsa temple.
tips: Autumn foliage is spectacular but very busy — go early.
Take the cable car for big views without the full climb.
Bring layers; mountain weather changes fast.

abai.name: Abai Village
abai.blurb: A seaside village reached by a hand-pulled ferry.
intro: Abai Village in Sokcho was settled by refugees from the north and is famous for its hand-pulled ‘gaetbae’ raft-ferry across the channel.
It is known for Abai sundae and squid dishes, and as a filming spot for hit Korean dramas.
tips: Ride the hand-pulled ferry across the inlet.
Try Abai sundae (stuffed sausage) and squid sundae.
Combine it with Sokcho Beach and the fish market.

ihwa.name: Ihwa Mural Village
ihwa.blurb: A steep hillside of murals near Naksan.
intro: Ihwa Mural Village climbs the slope below Naksan Park, its stairways and walls brightened with murals and art installations.
From the top there are wide views over the rooftops of old Seoul.
tips: It is a residential area — keep noise down and respect homes.
Combine it with a walk on the Naksan section of the old city wall.
Wear comfortable shoes for the steep lanes.

igidae.name: Igidae Coastal Walk
igidae.blurb: A rugged cliffside trail along the sea.
intro: Igidae is a coastal park in Busan with a rocky cliff trail and a suspension bridge, looking across the water to the Gwangan Bridge and the Haeundae skyline.
It links along the shore toward the Oryukdo Skywalk.
tips: Wear good shoes — parts are rocky with stairs.
The Gwangan Bridge views are best in the late afternoon.
You can walk on toward the Oryukdo Skywalk.

hyeopjae.name: Hyeopjae Beach
hyeopjae.blurb: White sand and turquoise water on Jeju’s west.
intro: Hyeopjae is one of Jeju’s prettiest beaches — white sand, shallow turquoise water and a view of Biyangdo island offshore.
The Hallim Park gardens and caves sit right next door.
tips: The water is shallow and calm — good for families.
Sunset over Biyangdo island is lovely.
Pair it with Hallim Park next door.

nambu-market.name: Jeonju Nambu Market
nambu-market.blurb: A traditional market with a youthful night hall.
intro: Nambu Market is Jeonju’s big traditional market — busy by day with produce and street food, and known for its ‘Youth Mall’ of young vendors upstairs.
On weekend nights a night market fills the aisles with food stalls.
tips: Come hungry — it is one of Jeonju’s best street-food spots.
Check for the weekend night market.
It is a short walk from the Hanok Village.

national-museum-korea.name: National Museum of Korea
national-museum-korea.blurb: Korea's largest museum — free entry to millennia of art and history.
intro: The National Museum of Korea in Yongsan is the country's flagship museum, tracing Korean history from prehistory through the Joseon era across vast, well-labelled galleries.
General admission is free and English signage makes it easy for first-time visitors.
tips: General admission is free; some special exhibitions are ticketed.
Don't miss the Pensive Bodhisattva room and the tall stone pagoda in the main hall.
It sits inside Yongsan Family Park — pair it with a riverside walk.

seoul-forest.name: Seoul Forest
seoul-forest.blurb: A big riverside park with a deer enclosure, gardens and café streets nearby.
intro: Seoul Forest is a large park east of the city centre, with wooded walking paths, a deer enclosure, water gardens and open lawns popular for picnics.
It sits beside the Han River and the trendy Seongsu café district.
tips: Free to enter and open year-round.
Walk or cycle the Han River path straight from the park.
Seongsu's cafés and pop-up stores are a short walk away.

beomeosa.name: Beomeosa Temple
beomeosa.blurb: A serene Silla-era temple on the wooded slopes of Geumjeongsan.
intro: Beomeosa is one of Busan's most important Buddhist temples, founded in the Silla era on the forested slopes of Geumjeongsan.
Its halls, stone pagoda and mountain setting feel a world away from the city's beaches.
tips: Combine it with a hike on Geumjeongsan or a walk along the old fortress wall.
Dress modestly — it's an active temple.
Take the subway to Beomeosa Station, then a short bus or uphill walk.

songjeong-beach.name: Songjeong Beach
songjeong-beach.blurb: A relaxed sandy beach popular for beginner surfing, just east of Haeundae.
intro: Songjeong is a calmer, more local beach just east of Haeundae, with gentle waves that make it Busan's favourite spot for first-time surfers.
Surf shops, cafés and the scenic Blueline Park coastal rail are all close by.
tips: Surf schools rent boards and run lessons in season.
The Blueline Park coastal rail runs between Songjeong and Haeundae.
It's quieter than Haeundae, especially on weekdays.

seopjikoji.name: Seopjikoji
seopjikoji.blurb: A grassy coastal cape with low cliffs, a lighthouse and spring canola fields.
intro: Seopjikoji is a grassy cape on Jeju's eastern coast, with easy paths along low cliffs, a white lighthouse and views back to Seongsan Ilchulbong.
In spring the surrounding fields turn bright yellow with canola blossom.
tips: Pair it with Seongsan Ilchulbong, which is close by.
Spring canola season and clear days are the most scenic.
The walk out to the lighthouse is easy and mostly flat.

seokguram.name: Seokguram Grotto
seokguram.blurb: A UNESCO granite grotto sheltering a serene seated Buddha above Bulguksa.
intro: Seokguram is a Silla-era stone grotto high on Tohamsan above Bulguksa, sheltering a magnificent seated Buddha ringed by carved guardians and bodhisattvas.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed together with Bulguksa temple.
tips: Visit it together with Bulguksa — they share the same mountain and heritage listing.
The main Buddha is viewed through glass to protect it, and photography inside is restricted.
Sunrise over the eastern ridges is famous here.

lotte-world.name: Lotte World
lotte-world.blurb: A huge theme park with an indoor 'Adventure' dome and an outdoor 'Magic Island' by a lake.
intro: Lotte World is one of Seoul's biggest theme parks — a covered indoor section that's great whatever the weather, plus an outdoor 'Magic Island' with rides around a lake.
It's easy to reach by subway and pairs with Lotte World Tower and Seokchon Lake right next door.
tips: Weekdays are far quieter than weekends.
It's right by Jamsil Station and Lotte World Tower.
The indoor area is a lifesaver on a rainy or very hot day.

namdaemun-market.name: Namdaemun Market
namdaemun-market.blurb: Korea's largest traditional market — street food, goods and bargains.
intro: Namdaemun is Korea's largest traditional market, a maze of alleys packed with clothes, kitchenware, accessories and some of Seoul's best street food.
It runs day and night and sits right by Namdaemun gate and Myeongdong.
tips: Come hungry — the food alleys are the highlight (try the hotteok and kalguksu).
Haggling is normal for goods, less so for food.
It's a short walk from Myeongdong and Seoul Station.

yongdusan.name: Yongdusan Park & Busan Tower
yongdusan.blurb: A hilltop park crowned by Busan Tower, with panoramic views over the port.
intro: Yongdusan Park sits on a hill in the middle of downtown Busan, topped by Busan Tower with sweeping views over the harbour and city.
It's steps from Nampo-dong, Gukje Market and the Jagalchi fish market.
tips: Go up the tower near sunset for the best light.
Escalators from Nampo-dong save you the climb.
Pair it with Gukje Market and Jagalchi nearby.

cheonjeyeon.name: Cheonjeyeon Waterfall
cheonjeyeon.blurb: A lush three-tier waterfall with a scenic 'Fairy Bridge' near Jungmun.
intro: Cheonjeyeon is a three-tier waterfall set in dense subtropical forest on Jeju's south coast, linked by shady paths and the ornate Seonimgyo 'fairy bridge'.
It sits beside the Jungmun resort area.
tips: Don't mix it up with Cheonjiyeon — this is the three-tier one near Jungmun.
The top tier flows mainly after rain; the lower tiers are reliable.
Combine it with Jungmun beach and the Jusangjeolli cliffs.

sanbangsan.name: Sanbangsan
sanbangsan.blurb: A dramatic bell-shaped lava dome with a cliffside cave temple and sea views.
intro: Sanbangsan is a striking bell-shaped lava dome on Jeju's southwest coast, with a cliff grotto temple (Sanbanggulsa) part-way up and wide views over the sea.
The Yongmeori coast right below makes an easy half-day.
tips: The climb to the grotto temple is short but steep.
Pair it with the Yongmeori coastal walk below.
It's especially pretty with the canola fields in spring.

woljeonggyo.name: Woljeonggyo Bridge
woljeonggyo.blurb: A beautifully reconstructed Silla-era covered wooden bridge, stunning at night.
intro: Woljeonggyo is a reconstructed Silla-era wooden bridge over the Namcheon stream in Gyeongju, with an elegant pavilion-roofed walkway.
It's most photogenic in the evening, lit up and reflected in the water.
tips: Come after dark for the illuminated reflection.
It's an easy walk or bike ride from Gyeongju's royal tomb park.
Free to cross and open into the evening.

incheon-chinatown.name: Incheon Chinatown
incheon-chinatown.blurb: Korea's largest Chinatown — birthplace of jjajangmyeon, with painted alleys and street snacks.
intro: Incheon Chinatown, right by the port, is Korea's oldest and largest Chinatown — a colourful maze of Chinese restaurants, bakeries and mural-lined stairways.
It's the birthplace of jjajangmyeon (black-bean noodles), and the Jjajangmyeon Museum tells the story.
tips: Try jjajangmyeon and freshly-steamed gonggal-ppang bread.
Walk up to the Samgukji mural street and the fairy-tale village next door.
It's a short walk from Incheon Station on Line 1.

songdo-central-park.name: Songdo Central Park
songdo-central-park.blurb: A sleek waterfront park with a saltwater canal, framed by Songdo's skyline.
intro: Songdo Central Park is the green heart of Incheon's futuristic Songdo district — a landscaped park built around a seawater canal, with skyscrapers rising on every side.
You can rent a pedal boat or hop on a water taxi along the canal.
tips: It's especially striking at night when the towers light up.
Rent a boat on the canal, or walk the full loop.
Reachable on Incheon subway Line 1.

wolmido.name: Wolmido
wolmido.blurb: A breezy seaside boardwalk with rides, cafés, seagulls and sunset views.
intro: Wolmido is Incheon's seaside playground — a waterfront promenade lined with cafés, an old-school amusement area, and boats where seagulls follow you for snacks.
It's a favourite for a sunset stroll and fresh seafood.
tips: Feeding the seagulls from the ferry deck is a Wolmido tradition.
Come for sunset and stay for the seaside cafés.
A short bus ride from Incheon Station.

eurwangni-beach.name: Eurwangni Beach
eurwangni-beach.blurb: A sandy sunset beach on Yeongjong Island, minutes from Incheon Airport.
intro: Eurwangni is a gentle sandy beach on Yeongjong Island, just minutes from Incheon Airport — a handy first or last stop, or an easy escape from Seoul.
It's known for shallow water, seafood restaurants and west-coast sunsets.
tips: Great for a layover or your first or last night near the airport.
Sunset here is the highlight.
Pair it with nearby Muui Island.

war-memorial.name: War Memorial of Korea
war-memorial.blurb: A vast, free museum of Korean military history with an outdoor weapons park.
intro: The War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan is a large, free museum tracing Korea's military history from ancient times through the Korean War, with moving memorial halls.
Its outdoor plaza displays tanks, aircraft and ships that kids and history buffs love.
tips: General admission is free.
The outdoor aircraft-and-tank park is a hit with kids.
It's near Itaewon and Samgakji Station.

banpo-hangang.name: Banpo Hangang Park
banpo-hangang.blurb: A Han River park famous for the Banpo Bridge Moonlight Rainbow Fountain.
intro: Banpo Hangang Park stretches along the Han River beside Banpo Bridge, home to the Moonlight Rainbow Fountain — a light-and-water show that arcs off the bridge on summer evenings.
By day it's a favourite for picnics, bikes and convenience-store ramyeon by the water.
tips: Check the fountain show times before you go — it's seasonal and runs in the evening.
Grab ramyeon and snacks from the riverside convenience store.
Rent a bike or a picnic mat and relax like the locals.
